correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge1\) and \(t\ge2\) with the stated independent uniform priority law, a perfect matching is stable iff its chosen student at school s_i is maximal in the intersection among the remaining students. The if-and-only-if proof handles all blocking pairs, and every maximal choice extends. The exact mean factors by school independence and permutation exchangeability, while uniqueness factors by conditional one-maximal-choice events; for t random permutations the local maximal count follows from an exact t-dimensional integral and the uniqueness chance from common first-rank agreement. The fixed-t logarithmic asymptotic uses an explicit integrable dominated-convergence majorant. One exact script independently cross-checks direct blocking-pair enumeration and recursive maximal-choice enumeration for the \(n=3,t=2\) global case (46656 profiles); a second script separately checks local random-order maximal-element identities and smaller controls. Verification scripts executed successfully; no finite experiment is used as proof for arbitrary n.

The school-priority intersection equivalence is known from Kitahara–Okumura 2023/2026 and the expected local number of random Pareto maxima is classical Bentley et al. 1978; both are expressly credited, rather than appropriated. Pittel 2019 randomizes preferences on both sides and does not directly cover the perfectly correlated common student order. value.rationale: A natural and economically meaningful source of assignment-selection discretion is simultaneous school priority criteria. The theorem is an all-market-size structural factorization, not a narrow table: for two independent criteria, the expected number of admissible stable assignments is product H_m while uniqueness shrinks as 1/n!, quantitatively contrasting with the unique common-preference stable assignment under one strict criterion. It is a reproducible benchmark for fairness constraints and how priority disagreement expands the feasible allocation set. The model assumptions and absence of concentration results are explicit.
